data.body:
The gap is wider than submit, and the earlier framing of this ticket understated it.

`rebar-review-bot` also lacks **`forgeCommitter`**, so it cannot upload a patchset whose committer is anyone other than itself. A push with the bot credential is rejected at the ref advertisement:

```
remote: ERROR: commit 0d9ad5b: email address joeoakhart@navapbc.com is not registered
        in your account, and you lack 'forge committer' permission.
remote: The following addresses are currently registered:
remote:    rebar-review-bot@rebar.solutions.navateam.com
 ! [remote rejected] HEAD -> refs/for/main (commit 0d9ad5b: invalid committer)
```

**Why this was not noticed earlier.** It looked at first like a server-side regression, because pushes had been succeeding all day with an unchanged committer identity. They had not been succeeding as the bot. Querying the uploader on every existing patchset settles it:

| change | patchsets | uploader |
|---|---|---|
| 2984 | ps1-ps5 | Administrator |
| 2986 | ps1-ps2 | Administrator |
| 2987 | ps1 | Administrator |

Every patchset on every change was uploaded by `Administrator`, which is in the `Administrators` group and therefore holds `forgeCommitter`. No ACL changed; the bot credential had simply never been used for a push before. Nothing on the server moved.

**Current permission state, from the live config.**

- Account: `rebar-review-bot`, `_account_id` 1000002, tagged `SERVICE_USER`. One registered email, `rebar-review-bot@rebar.solutions.navateam.com`, and no secondary emails.
- Groups: `Registered Users`, `Anonymous Users`, `Service Users`, and its own per-user group. Not `Contributors`.
- On `All-Projects` `refs/heads/*`: `forgeAuthor` is granted to `Registered Users`, but `forgeCommitter` only to `Project-Owners` and `Administrators`.
- On the `rebar` project: `push` to `refs/for/refs/heads/*` is granted to `Registered Users`, which is why the bot reaches the commit-validation stage at all before being refused there.
- On `refs/heads/*`: `submit` is granted only to `Administrators` and one other group, matching the submit refusal already recorded here.

So the bot can create a change, but cannot upload one authored by a human and cannot submit. Both operations currently require the admin credential, which makes `Administrator` the owner of every change and erases the distinction between the account that proposes work and the account that lands it.

Three remedies are possible and they are not equivalent: register the human committer address as a secondary email on the bot account; grant `forgeCommitter` to `Service Users` or to a group containing the bot; or keep committer identity as the bot's own and stop forging it, which would change what the DCO sign-off attests. Choosing between them is a human decision and is not being made here.
